question.prompt: The sequence \[ \begin{gathered} \log_{12} 162, \ \log_{12} x, \ \log_{12} y, \\ \ \log_{12} z, \ \log_{12} 1250 \end{gathered} \] is an arithmetic progression. What is \(x?\)

solutions.explanation:
There are four equal gaps between the five terms. Let their common difference be \(d\). All logarithm arguments must be positive. Using the first and fifth terms,
\[
4d=\log_{12}1250-\log_{12}162
=\log_{12}\left(\frac{1250}{162}\right).
\]
The ratio inside the logarithm is a fourth power:
\[
\frac{1250}{162}=\frac{625}{81}=\left(\frac53\right)^4.
\]
The logarithm power rule therefore gives \(4d=4\log_{12}(5/3)\), so \(d=\log_{12}(5/3)\).

The second term is one gap beyond the first, giving
\[
\log_{12}x
=\log_{12}162+\log_{12}\frac53
=\log_{12}270.
\]
Raising \(12\) to both sides yields \(x=270\). This value is positive; the full list of arguments \(162,270,450,750,1250\) has common ratio \(5/3\), so their logarithms do have equal differences. Thus the answer is \(\boxed{270}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Find the common logarithmic difference
